title: Filet lace
summary: Filet lace begins with a knotted net of square meshes. The maker darns cotton through chosen squares, so the solid stitches draw the picture and the open net becomes the ground. It was used for curtains, bed covers and borders.
howToPlay: Pick a cotton colour from the spools and a darning shape from the tray.
Touch a square of the net to darn that shape there; it is mirrored across and down.
Copy the chart shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The chart is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you darn is also darned on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its cotton colour both match the chart you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Darned net of this kind has been made in Europe since the Renaissance, where it is often called lacis, and filet work was practised in France and Italy. The same chart-based method is still used today for table linen and curtain borders.
